articles.title: Jewel tones for the sangeet
articles.summary: Emerald and deep green read richly under evening lights. Pair with polki or uncut stones and keep the neckline clean so the jewellery stands out.

articles.title: The sangeet edit
articles.summary: Shararas and lighter lehengas are the practical choice for dancing. Sequins catch stage lighting; choose heels with a block for comfort.

articles.title: Light for the dance floor
articles.summary: Pre-draped sarees and mirror work keep you comfortable through long functions. Oxidised silver suits pastel and mint palettes.

articles.title: Red returns to the mandap
articles.summary: Classic red is back for the pheras. Heavier lehengas need early fittings; plan at least 14 to 16 weeks for hand embroidery.

articles.title: Reception looks that photograph well
articles.summary: Ivory and gold photograph beautifully under warm lights. Gown-lehenga hybrids are easier to move in for long receptions.

articles.title: Haldi brights
articles.summary: Choose fabrics you don't mind staining. Floral jewellery is light, cheap and photographs well.

articles.title: Pastels for day functions
articles.summary: Pastel pinks and greens suit daytime mehendi. Gota work is light and breathable for outdoor settings.

articles.title: The groom's wardrobe, function by function
articles.summary: Match the bride's palette rather than her exact colour. Velvet bandhgalas work for winter evenings; linen for haldi.

articles.title: A guide to Udaipur weddings
articles.summary: Lake-facing palaces book 9 to 12 months ahead for peak season (Nov to Feb). Boat transfers add to logistics; plan guest movement early.

articles.title: Beach weddings in Goa
articles.summary: Sunset pheras are popular. Sound restrictions after 10 pm apply at many venues; plan the sangeet indoors or earlier.
